steps.label: Do Now: The Purpose of the CPU (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: The Purpose of the CPU (1 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the exam ask for the CPU's job, and not what it is called?Show the answer

Knowing the name shows you remember it. Saying the job shows you understand what it does.

Recap of the last lesson. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2025, Question 3(b). A computer has a central processing unit (CPU), memory and secondary storage.

items.prompt: State the purpose of the CPU in the computer.
scheme: To execute or process instructions
To perform the fetch-decode-execute cycle
items.guidance: One mark for either point. "It processes data and instructions" earns the mark. "It is the brain of the computer" earns no mark.

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: stating a purpose

steps.text: A similar question. A greenhouse has a temperature sensor. State the purpose of the sensor.
steps.visual: "purpose" means: what job does it do?

steps.text: "State the purpose" asks for the job it does, not what it looks like or where it is.
A sensor's job: it measures something and sends the reading on. Here: it measures the temperature and sends it to the microprocessor.
An answer such as "it is a small part of the greenhouse" earns nothing: it does not say what the sensor does.
steps.visual: a description is not a job

steps.text: Now do the same for the CPU: one short sentence that says the job it does with instructions.

steps.label: Do Now: A Library Microprocessor (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: A Library Microprocessor (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a library use a microprocessor for this job, and not a person with a notebook?Show the answer

It is fast, works all day, and does not make counting mistakes.

Recap of the last lesson. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 2(g). A library has a self-checkout system. It is linked to a stock control system that is updated every time a book is borrowed. A microprocessor is used in the stock control system to update the stock.

items.prompt: Explain the role of the microprocessor in this system and how it is used to update the stock when a book is borrowed.
scheme: It receives data from the self-checkout system
It compares the book data received to stored book data
... that is a database of stock
If the book is found it decrements (takes 1 off) the book stock
If the book is not found an error message is displayed
items.guidance: Any three, one mark each. The "database of stock" mark needs the compare point first. "Updates the stock" alone earns no mark: it must say the stock goes down by 1.
items.modelAnswer: It receives the book data from the self-checkout. It compares it with the stored book data. If the book is found, it takes 1 off the stock.

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: a microprocessor in a system

steps.text: A similar question. A car park barrier has a microprocessor. A driver scans a ticket. Explain how the microprocessor decides if the barrier opens.
Input: the microprocessor receives data. Here, the ticket number from the scanner.
Process: it compares the data with data it has stored. Here, the list of tickets that have been paid.
steps.visual: compares with the stored list

steps.text: Output, part 1: if the ticket is found, it sends a signal to open the barrier.
Output, part 2: if not found, it shows an error message. Each "if" is a separate mark.
Now do the same for the library: what data does the microprocessor receive, what does it compare it with, and what happens if the book is found, or not found?
steps.visual: receive, compare, if found, if not found

steps.label: CPU Components
steps.content:
3.1 Computer Architecture

CPU Components

Year 10

  • Today: the parts inside the CPU, and why each one is needed.
  • The ALU and the CU: the part that does the maths and the part in charge.
  • Five registers: PC, MAR, MDR, CIR and ACC.
Think → Pair → ShareLast lesson, the CPU ran a program stored in memory. Predict: what does the CPU need to remember while it runs a program?Show the answer

Where the next instruction is, what it is doing now, and the answer so far. Something inside the CPU must hold each of these.

steps.label: The ALU and the CU
steps.content:
The ALU and the CU

Think → Pair → ShareA program says: LOAD 5, then ADD 6. Predict: why might a CPU have one part that does the adding, and a different part that reads the program and decides what happens next?Show the worked answer

Two different jobs. One part only has to calculate. The other is in charge: it works out what each instruction means and sends signals to make the right parts do it.

  • ALU: arithmetic logic unit. It carries out calculations (such as 25 + 17) and logical operations (such as: is 41 bigger than 30?).
  • The ALU stores the result in a register called the accumulator.
  • CU: control unit. It sends control signals to manage how data and instructions move through the CPU.
  • The CU decodes each instruction: it works out what the instruction means.
  • A CPU built this way, running a program stored in memory, has a Von Neumann architecture.
CPU
CU control unit
CIR current instruction
ALU arithmetic logic unit
ACC accumulator
PC program counter
MAR memory address register
MDR memory data register

steps.label: Predict: ALU or CU?
steps.content:
Predict: ALU or CU?

Think → Pair → ShareBefore you answer, why should you ask "is this maths, or is this being in charge?"Show the answer

Every job in the CPU is one or the other, so that one question tells you which unit does it.

The program LOAD 5, ADD 6, OUTPUT is running.

items.prompt: The CPU must work out that ADD 6 means "add the number stored at address 6". Which part does this?
items.explain: Working out what an instruction means is decoding. The CU decodes instructions. The ALU only does the adding once it is told to.

items.prompt: Address 6 holds 17 and the CPU holds 25. Which part works out 25 + 17?
items.explain: Adding is a calculation, so the ALU does it. The result, 42, goes into the accumulator.

steps.label: Activity 1: Who Does This Job?
steps.content:
Activity 1: Who Does This Job?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do the PC and the MAR get mixed up?Show the answer

Both hold an address. The PC holds the address of the next instruction; the MAR holds the address being read or written right now.

Pick the part of the CPU that does each job. One check per set, and a mistake means it does not count. Three levels: ALU or CU, the registers, then all seven.

steps.label: Why Does the CPU Need Registers?
steps.content:
Why Does the CPU Need Registers?

Think → Pair → ShareMain memory holds the whole program, but it is outside the CPU. Predict: why does the CPU also keep a few values in tiny stores of its own?Show the worked answer

Memory is slower to reach. The CPU keeps what it needs right now, such as the next address and the current instruction, close by, so it can work fast.

  • A register is a tiny, very fast store inside the CPU. It holds one data item, address or instruction for a short time.
  • PC (program counter): the address of the next instruction.
  • MAR (memory address register): the address memory is about to read or write.
  • MDR (memory data register): the data or instruction that has just come from memory, or is about to go to it.
  • CIR (current instruction register): the instruction being decoded and carried out now. It is part of the CU.
  • ACC (accumulator): the result of a calculation from the ALU, part-way through the program.
CPU
CU control unit
CIR current instruction
ALU arithmetic logic unit
ACC accumulator
PC program counter
MAR memory address register
MDR memory data register

steps.content:
Watch One Instruction

Think → Pair → ShareWatch what goes into the MAR each time. Predict: why does the CPU put the address into the MAR, and not just read memory using the PC?Show the worked answer

The PC must keep the address of the next instruction. The MAR is used for every address memory reads, including data addresses such as 5 in LOAD 5. Using the PC would lose the place in the program.

steps.label: Predict: What Do the Registers Hold?
steps.content:
Predict: What Do the Registers Hold?

Think → Pair → ShareStraight after an instruction is taken from memory, why do the MDR and the CIR hold the same thing?Show the answer

The instruction arrives in the MDR from memory, then it is copied into the CIR so the CU can decode it.

The same memory: 0 LOAD 5, 1 ADD 6, 2 OUTPUT, 3 STOP; address 5 holds 30 and address 6 holds 12. LOAD 5 has finished, so the ACC holds 30 and the PC holds 1.

items.prompt: The CPU takes the next instruction from memory. What does the MAR hold first?
items.explain: The address in the PC (1) is copied into the MAR, so memory reads address 1, where ADD 6 is stored.

items.prompt: Once ADD 6 is in the CIR, what does the PC hold?
items.explain: The PC went up by 1 when the instruction was taken from memory. It now holds 2, the address of OUTPUT, the next instruction.

items.prompt: ADD 6 has been carried out. What does the ACC hold?
items.explain: The MDR gets 12 from address 6. The ALU works out 30 + 12 = 42 and puts it in the ACC.

steps.label: Activity 2: Watch the Registers
steps.content:
Activity 2: Watch the Registers

Think → Pair → ShareWhy are there two registers for memory, the MAR and the MDR?Show the answer

One holds where to look (the address); the other holds what was found there (the data or instruction).

Predict what each register will hold, then run the CPU one small step at a time to see why. Three levels; a wrong box means the round does not count.

steps.label: Exam Questions: Name the Part
steps.content:
Exam Questions: Name the Part

Think → Pair → ShareWhy do these questions say "identify" or "state", and not "describe"?Show the answer

They want only the name, for 1 mark. A long description takes time and earns nothing more.

Four real 1-mark questions. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11 November 2021 Q6(b); 0478/11 November 2023 Q1(c); 0478/11 June 2025 Q5(b); 0478/13 November 2025 Q2(b)(ii).

Total: 4 marks

steps.label: Exam Questions: The ALU and the CU
steps.content:
Exam Questions: The ALU and the CU

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must each point in a "describe" answer be a different idea?Show the answer

Each mark is for one point. Saying the same idea twice in new words earns only one mark.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13 June 2024 Q8(c) and 0478/13 November 2025 Q2(b)(i). Each "describe" mark is a separate point.

items.prompt: One component in the CPU is the arithmetic logic unit (ALU). Describe the purpose of the ALU.
scheme: To execute instructions
To perform calculations (or an example, such as adding)
To perform logical operations (or an example, such as comparing)
To store interim results of calculations
It stores, reads or writes data to or from the accumulator
items.guidance: Any three, one mark each. An example of a calculation (adds two numbers) earns the calculation mark; an example of a logical operation (compares two numbers) earns the logic mark. "It does maths" is a calculation point.
items.modelAnswer: It performs calculations and logical operations. It stores the results in the accumulator.

items.prompt: The CPU has a control unit (CU). Describe the role of the CU in the CPU.
scheme: It sends control signals to other components
... using the control bus
... to manage the flow of data through the CPU
It decodes an instruction
... using an instruction set
items.guidance: Any three, one mark each. The "control bus" and "flow of data" marks follow the control signals point. The "instruction set" mark follows the decodes point. "It controls the computer" alone earns no mark.
items.modelAnswer: It sends control signals to manage the flow of data through the CPU. It decodes instructions.

steps.label: Exam Question: ALU, CU or Main Memory?
steps.content:
Exam Question: ALU, CU or Main Memory?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a CPU need one part that calculates and a different part that controls?Show the answer

They are different jobs. Keeping them apart means each part can be simple and fast.

Adapted from Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2021, Question 10(a). Three components are the arithmetic logic unit (ALU), control unit (CU) and random access memory (RAM), the main memory. Which component does each statement apply to?

items.prompt: Stores data and instructions before they enter the CPU.
items.explain: Main memory (RAM) holds the program and its data. They go into the CPU when they are needed.

items.prompt: Contains a register called the accumulator.
items.explain: The accumulator is part of the ALU: it holds the ALU's results.

items.prompt: Manages the transmission of data and instructions to the correct components.
items.explain: Managing where data and instructions go is control, so it is the CU.
Calculations are done by the ALU.

steps.label: Exam Questions: The Registers
steps.content:
Exam Questions: The Registers

Think → Pair → ShareWhy should you read a register name twice before you answer?Show the answer

Some names look alike, such as MAR and MDR, but they do different jobs.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12 March 2021 Q8(b)(i) and 0478/11 November 2023 Q1(e). The CPU contains registers, including the program counter (PC) and the memory data register (MDR).

items.prompt: Describe the role of the Program Counter.
scheme: It holds the address ...
... of the next (or current) instruction
items.guidance: One mark for holds an address, one for of the next instruction. "Counts the instructions" earns no mark.
items.modelAnswer: It holds the address of the next instruction.

items.prompt: Describe the role of the MDR in the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
scheme: It stores data ...
... that has been fetched from memory, or is to be written to memory
items.guidance: One mark for stores data (or an instruction), one for that has been fetched from memory or is about to be written to memory. "Stores the address" earns no mark: that is the MAR.
items.modelAnswer: It stores data that has been fetched from memory.

items.prompt: Identify three other registers contained in the CPU.
scheme: Memory address register (MAR)
Program counter (PC)
Current instruction register (CIR)
Accumulator (ACC)
items.guidance: Any three, one mark each. The MDR is in the question, so it earns no mark. Abbreviations alone (MAR, PC, CIR, ACC) earn the marks.

steps.label: Exam Question: Definitions
steps.content:
Exam Question: Definitions

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must a definition be exact, even for 1 mark?Show the answer

The mark is for the one idea that makes this term different from every other term.

Adapted from Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2025, Question 5(a). Complete the definition for each term.

items.prompt: Current instruction register (CIR). Give its definition.
scheme: It stores the instruction that is being decoded or executed
items.guidance: One mark for holding the current instruction, or the instruction being decoded or executed. "Stores instructions" alone earns no mark: it must be the current one.
items.modelAnswer: It stores the instruction being decoded or executed.

scheme: It stores the result of interim calculations
items.guidance: One mark for storing the results of (interim) calculations, or the results from the ALU.
items.modelAnswer: It stores the result of interim calculations.
